title: Move four sealed cups of unknown weight without crushing or dropping them
instruction: Put all four cups on the tray upright.
context: Fast food and counter workers (about 3.8 million in the US, BLS 2024) hand over and bag sealed, lidded cups and pots many times an hour, and the cups look alike whatever they hold. Squeezed too hard a thin wall creases; gripped too lightly a full cup slides out. Friction alone holds a cup, so each pad must press at least m g / (2 mu): the heaviest cup needs more than the lightest one's wall can take. The four cups look the same but hold 20 to 400 g, and no single grip force moves all four intact: the robot must feel each cup's weight as it lifts and set its grip from that.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table top (x forward, y left). Four identical white cups (0.25 mm PETG wall, printed PLA base and seal; build in README), 7 cm across, 9 cm tall, straight sides, red foil seal recessed 6 mm below the rim, 1 cm bands drawn on the wall; 26 g empty, each filled with damp sand to a hidden mass from the seed (default seed 0: 120 g at (34, 21), 205 g at (22, 21), 45 g at (34, -21), 320 g at (22, -21)); all upright. A dark grey tray taped to the table, 21 x 28 cm outside (long side along y), 5 mm floor, 1 cm rims 2 cm tall, centred at (30, 0). Nothing else on the table. Arms start in the ready pose.
scoring: Per cup, 0.25 if: at some point it was 2 cm or more up, held for 0.5 s by a grip on its side wall alone (no robot contact on its base or seal meanwhile); that grip ended with it on the tray; at the end its base is inside the tray rim, it stands within 10 degrees of upright and no gripper holds it; and never during the trial did its wall crease or buckle, its base rise over 1 cm above the surface under it without a side-wall grip (dropped, slid out, scooped, stacked), it tilt past 30 degrees, share one gripper with another cup in the air, or leave the table. Touching the base or seal, or a slip along the fingers, costs nothing by itself. Score is the sum; 1.0 when all four (success, held 1 s).
reset_notes: A creased cup is used up: replace it with a fresh cup filled to the same mass. Fill masses for other seeds are listed in the README (CUPS_SEED); weigh each cup after filling. Stand the cups back on their taped marks.
fidelity: Approximate. Each cup wall is 8 rigid panels on radial spring slides (about 1,000 N/m under a pad), so a grip visibly presses it in. PhysX cannot buckle a shell: when the measured pad force exceeds the cup's buckling force for 12.5 ms, the panels take a dented rest position. Buckling force and pad friction (0.35) are those measured on built cups (README): 1.5 N at 20 g, 1.6 N at 60 g to 15 N at 400 g, linear between. Wall stiffness does not depend on fill. Fill is a rigid mass; tray fixed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0 (seed 0; also 1.0 on seeds 4 and 10)
